name: Dudák
summary: Czech Durak-family shedding game where each player has a personal trump suit and tries not to be last with cards.
rules_text: Dudak uses 32 German-suited cards, 8 each to 4 players (2-3 can play). On your turn if the central pile is empty you lead any card. If not empty you must beat the top card: with a higher card of same suit before you have declared trumps, afterwards also with any card of your personal trump suit. After beating you must play a second card of your choice on top. If you cannot or will not beat, you pick up: before declaring trumps you may uncover cards one by one from the pile into your hand until you find one you can beat, then beat it and continue; if you empty the pile you take it and your turn ends. After declaring trumps you must take the whole pile if you don't beat. At start of your turn you may declare any still-undeclared suit as your permanent trump for the deal; the last player gets the last suit. If you beat with your last card the whole pile is discarded. First to empty hand drops out; last player holding cards loses.
rating_reason: Czech beating shedding game like Durak, strategic hidden hands
